# Stephen Green

::: {.hero-subtitle}
Principal Research Fellow &middot; University of Nottingham
:::

I am a physicist working on **machine learning for gravitational waves** and **black hole perturbation theory**. My group develops [simulation-based inference methods](research/sbi/) that can analyze gravitational-wave signals in seconds rather than days, and I work on [foundational problems in classical gravity](research/gravity/) including extreme mass-ratio inspirals, spacetime turbulence, and cosmological backreaction.

I hold a [UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship](https://www.ukri.org/news/68-new-future-leaders-fellows-awarded-104-million-in-the-eighth-round/) and am a member of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration and the LISA Consortium.

### Real-time inference for binary neutron star mergers using machine learning

::: {.pub-summary}
Led by Max Dax, this work demonstrates that neural posterior estimation can enable one-second inference for binary neutron star mergers --- complete parameter estimation including sky localization, crucial for multimessenger astronomy.
:::

::: {.section-label}
Research
:::

::: {.research-preview}
### [Machine Learning for Gravitational Waves](research/sbi/)

Amortized neural posteriors for fast and accurate parameter estimation of gravitational-wave signals. Developer of the [Dingo](https://github.com/dingo-gw/dingo) inference code.

[Read more &rarr;](research/sbi/){.read-more}
:::

::: {.research-preview}
### [Classical Gravity](research/gravity/)

Black hole perturbation theory and metric reconstruction. Nonlinear dynamics and turbulence in anti-de Sitter spacetime. Backreaction in cosmology.

[Read more &rarr;](research/gravity/){.read-more}
:::
